add.name: Supreme Halal Beef Jerky, Jalapeño Garlic

halal.certifier: Halal Food Standards Alliance of America (HFSAA)

evidence.label: Jerky review site Jerky Ingredients reports the company's facilities are HFSAA-certified and the beef is zabiha halal.
Trade press reports the brand uses 100% certified halal beef.

halal.summary: HFSAA is named as the certifier in a 2025 review. Not yet confirmed on HFSAA's own list.

evidence.label: Midamar sells it as zabiha halal beef jerky.
Midamar says it works with several certifiers, most often Islamic Services of America, and publishes its certificate.

halal.summary: Midamar is a long-standing halal brand and publishes a certificate, but we haven't matched this jerky to a named certifier yet.

add.name: Pacific Gold Halal Beef Jerky, Original

evidence.label: Costco lists "Halal" under the product's certifications; no certifier is named.

halal.summary: Pacific Gold's halal-labelled jerky. The retailer lists it as halal-certified but doesn't name the certifier.

add.name: Halal Mummified Jerky, Original Silver Nile

evidence.label: Jerky Ingredients reports the beef is certified halal by Halal Transactions of Omaha and the bag carries a halal mark (2018 review).

halal.summary: Halal Transactions of Omaha is named as the certifier, but our source is from 2018, so check the current bag.

add.name: Sharifa Halal Beef Jerky, Black Pepper

evidence.label: Halal World Depot, a retailer, lists it among "100% Halal Certified" products; no certifier is named.

halal.summary: Sold as halal-certified, but we could not find which body certifies it.
